## Legend / conventions

- Source: `ULTIMATE MASTER GOAL — Production Universal Financial Control Plane.md` (repo root; PART 1–249 plus STAGE 0–19). Every PART appears at least once below.
- ID scheme: `R-<PART>-<n>` (PART zero-padded to 3 digits, e.g. `R-017-3` = third requirement of PART 17). Stage-derived rows use `R-S<stage>-<n>`. Rows for the **productization** goal (`product_goal.md`, repo root) use `R-PG<section>-<n>` — its sections are numbered independently of the original goal's PARTs, so `R-PG038-1` (its §38, admin product support) and `R-038-1` (PART 38, the Settlement Compiler) are different requirements and the prefix is what keeps them apart. A PART is split into several rows whenever it contains separately testable requirements.
- Requirement text is a compressed restatement that keeps numbers, state names, field lists and forbidden items. Where the goal lists many items, the list is kept verbatim (comma-separated) so the row is auditable without re-reading the goal.
- Implementation path / Test proving it name locations in the single Go module `github.com/nodal/controlplane` (layout of PART 14). A path without a prefix exists on disk and was verified on the date in the change log; a `planned:` prefix marks a location that does not exist yet. Every path and every test name in this file was re-checked against the working tree on 2026-09-06, and the test-name half is now checked continuously rather than on an afternoon: `TestDocs_EveryTestTheyNameExists` requires every `Test*`/`Fuzz*` name cited here to resolve to a declaration that exists. The count that used to stand here — "all 609 Go test-function references" — has been removed rather than updated: it was a hand-count whose counting rule was never written down, so nobody could reproduce it to say whether it had gone stale, and a number nobody can check is worth less than the property a test enforces (F-111). Every unprefixed path existed on disk on that date. Where something is absent the row says so in words, rather than leaving a stale `planned:` on a location that has since been built.
- Operational evidence: `n/a` when the requirement is proven by tests alone; `planned: <what>` when runtime/operational evidence is also needed for VERIFIED.
- Blocker column references `docs/build/BLOCKERS.md`, which is the authoritative definition of every ID below (BLOCKERS.md is where each blocker's current status lives; this table restates only what each id means). The table below is a summary only.
- Initial state: every row is NOT_STARTED except PART 4 hard exclusions and PART 13 premature-technology items, which are DEFERRED_OUT_OF_SCOPE by definition (each such row names the interface kept open so a later implementation remains possible, per PART 4 "design interfaces so later implementations remain possible"). Stage 0 items already evidenced in MASTER_BUILD_STATE.md are the first candidates for state updates by the build owner.
- BLOCKED_EXTERNAL is used only per PART 167 (software + tests + gate complete, external item genuinely unavailable). A row that merely references an EB-xxx blocker but has no code is still NOT_STARTED.

| R-180-1 | PART 180 | Rate limits: user API, auth, quote, strategy event, model budget, provider protection; rate limiting is not financial authority; Redis acceptable for counters | VERIFIED | internal/ratelimit (fixed-window limiter; Redis store with an atomic Lua INCR+PEXPIRE; memory store; chi middleware emitting RateLimit / Retry-After headers and problem+json) is applied by cmd/api per route class -- user API, auth, quote, command -- with documented defaults that are configurable per environment and cannot be disabled in production. WHERE the counters live is configuration: CP_RATELIMIT_BACKEND selects memory or redis, config.Validate refuses memory for an HTTP binary in STAGING/PROD, and cmd/api PINGs Redis before the server starts rather than discovering the outage on the first request. The Redis-backed limiter fails CLOSED; the process-local one fails open, which is a statement about a store that cannot fail. Until F-82 nothing constructed a Redis client at all and cmd/api chose the memory store, so with api_autoscaling.min_capacity = 3 every limit was enforced three times over -- the Redis integration tests cited here proved the store worked, not that anything used it. It is documented as not financial authority: the order-rate budget lives in internal/risk against persisted intents | internal/ratelimit unit, property, concurrency and Redis integration tests `-race` (the Redis test sat in an untagged file until F-57, where `make unit` skipped it for want of a server and the integration enumeration -- which selects on the build tag -- never reached the package; it is now `redis_integration_test.go` and the CI job starts Redis). Multi-replica behaviour, which is the only condition under which the store choice matters, is covered by TestReplicas_ProcessLocalCountersMultiplyTheBudget (three memory stores admit 30 against a limit of 10), TestReplicas_OneSharedStoreEnforcesOneBudget (10), TestReplicas_ASharedStoreOutageDoesNotBecomeAProcessLocalLimit (every request reaches the failed store, each is refused, the middleware answers 500) and, against a real server, TestIntegration_RedisStore's three-client case. cmd/api TestParseLimit, TestRateLimitsAreConfigurableWithTheDocumentedDefaults, TestRateLimitsCannotBeDisabledInProduction and the TestRateLimitStore_* set (production refuses the process-local store; missing, malformed, plaintext-under-TLS and unreachable Redis each stop startup; no failure path returns a memory store). internal/config TestService_TheAPINeedsRedisOnlyWhenItsCountersAreShared and TestValidate_RedisTLSBelongsToWhoeverActuallyUsesRedis. internal/risk TestIntegration_CountOrders_FromPersistedIntents. | 2026-09-09 | **Per-service configuration dependencies.** `internal/config.Load` now takes a `config.Service` and a variable belonging to an external dependency is required only of a binary that declares it. Rows touching `CP_REDIS_*`, `CP_REDPANDA_*`, `CP_CLICKHOUSE_*`, `CP_TEMPORAL_*` and `CP_ARCHIVE_*` are unchanged in status: the variables, their parsing and their production TLS rules all still exist, and the only thing that moved is which binary is asked for them. Two findings recorded rather than fixed: **nothing in the repository constructs a Redis client** (`ratelimit.NewRedisStore` has no caller and `cmd/api` builds the in-memory store), which with `api_autoscaling.min_capacity = 3` makes every rate limit three times looser than configured and twelve times at maximum capacity; and `cmd/audit-worker`'s S3 Object Lock archive is still unwired, so its `DepArchive` declaration records where it is going rather than what it does today. | The dependency table in `internal/config/service.go` is an audit of what each binary CONSTRUCTS, cross-checked against what it LINKS: `go list -deps ./cmd/<name>` for the client libraries in each binary, and the composition roots for which of those are built. The two disagree in one place and it is the important one -- `cmd/api` links go-redis through `internal/ratelimit` and then chooses `NewMemoryStore`. Tests: `internal/config/service_test.go` (API starts in PROD with Redis/Redpanda/ClickHouse/Temporal absent; each dependency-declaring binary refuses to start without its own; malformed values fail closed for every binary; no service falls back to LOCAL defaults; `Load` refuses an undeclared service; the config hash distinguishes services), plus `TestLoad_DefaultsNeverApplyOutsideLocalTest` and `TestValidate_PresenceRulesBelongToTheServicesThatUseThem`, both now per service and computed from the same tables the loader uses. |
